evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: six-arm star with short side branches spaced along each arm, oxblood on clay; by shot-20s the branches have lengthened into a dense fern figure with the arms fully developed.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: one flat oxblood silhouette on a single rose-to-dark gradient, with no second layer, lighting or material; by shot-20s the same figure is denser but still one layer.
evidence.craft: shot-20s: dense hatching along the arms shimmers into moire and small debris specks sit at the arm tips; shot-02s: letters on the arms are crowded and some are mirrored.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: rose-clay ground with an oxblood six-arm dendrite, unlike the ochre-and-rust tiling of the recent nights in palette, silhouette and idea.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: the figure sits off-centre toward the top-left with letters running off-frame; shot-20s recentres the six-fold figure into a balanced end state.

pairwise_justification: shot-08s is one oxblood silhouette on a flat gradient, while the median's ochre and rust Penrose tiling subdivides into many tones by its late frame; the median wins the head-to-head on tonal richness.

critique.change: Add a subtle shaded material to the arms (a bevel or directional light falloff from the tip) so the side branches read as 3D growth rather than flat strokes at shot-20s.
Anti-alias the dense side-branch hatching at shot-20s, or thin it, so the arms stop shimmering into moire and the fine structure resolves cleanly.
Make the fixed-lag rule legible: at shot-08s place the letters of defect in one constant-spaced row behind the tip, instead of crowded glyphs scattered along the arms.
